# STRATO Parameter Register (Deliverable 5)

Project: STRATO (Spherical TRISO Analysis and Transport Operations). Register compiled 2026-11-06 from the verified Stage 1 audit notes (`01` to `08`, including each file's Verification log, whose corrections supersede the original text). No value in this register was invented, estimated or taken from memory. Every number traces to a printed page of a source PDF or to an evaluated nuclear data library queried during the audit.

Tables in this file are rendered from the machine-readable CSV files listed in Section 0.3, so the row identifiers (G-, A-, N-, Y-, TH-, E-) are the same in both places.

Data integration of 2026-11-25 (task `btcs-data-integration`). The three research additions (`data/reference/additions/research-diffusivity-sources.md`, `research-agr1-irradiation.md`, `research-release-data.md`, kept unchanged in structure as the source record) are merged below: new rows C15-01 to C15-13 and S20-01 to S20-10 (Tables 14a, 14b), the statements and the class of every coefficient (Sections 5.4 to 5.7), AGR-1 irradiation conditions (Tables 26a to 26f, Section 8.1), the derived fission-rate density (Section 8.2), the temperature histories TH-123 to TH-157 (Table 25a) and the release rows E-157 to E-540 (Tables 31a to 31h, Section 9.1). From this date the tables of Sections 4 to 9 are maintained in this file together with the CSV files; `scripts/data_register/render_register.py` and its template no longer reproduce them. The columns added by decision 44 are described in Section 0.6.

## 0. How to read this register

### 0.1 Rule on synthetic values

Synthetic, notional or "demonstration" values never appear here. The v1.0 synthetic case (`deliverables/synthetic_five_layer.toml`: radii 200 to 450 $\mathrm{\mu m}$, piecewise-constant $D$) and the VTB example inputs found in the repository review (kernel 425 $\mathrm{\mu m}$, 15.5 wt% enrichment, 700 °C) are deliberately excluded. Benchmark definitions that are synthetic by construction (CRP-6 sensitivity cases 1 to 5 and case 11) are included because they are printed specifications with published reference answers; they carry the class "specified (synthetic benchmark)".

### 0.2 Status and data-class vocabulary

| Status (CSV column `status`) | Meaning |
|---|---|
| verified | value read from the printed page (or library) by the audit and re-checked by the independent verifier |
| digitised | value read from a raster figure, either by pixel digitisation (R-dig, about $\pm 5$ % of value, validated against a printed table) or by visual reading (R-vis, about $\pm 10$ to 15 % on linear axes, about a factor 1.5 on log axes) |
| NOT VERIFIED | value, label or interpretation that could not be confirmed against a primary source; see Section 11 |

Data classes: **measured** (characterisation or release measurement), **M-UB** (measured upper bound or detection-limit statement), **design specification**, **benchmark specification**, **recommended/fitted correlation** (Arrhenius fits to irradiation and heating data), **model input set** (a code's chosen parameter set), **calculated** (computed in this register by the check script; never a source value), **evaluated** (nuclear data library).

Evidence classes (CSV column `evidence_class`, added by the B6 audit on 2026-11-06). The column `status` says whether a value was checked against its source; the column `evidence_class` says what kind of value it is. Every row of every CSV carries exactly one of the following.

| Evidence class | Meaning | May be used as |
|---|---|---|
| measured | experimental value printed in a table, in the text or in a vector figure | validation target |
| measured, digitised | experimental value read from a raster figure (status `digitised`) | validation target with the digitisation uncertainty of Section 0.2 |
| measured bound | upper bound or detection-limit statement ("<") | inequality constraint only, never a point value |
| literature correlation | Arrhenius fit from the literature, including the same fit reproduced as a code input set (Collin et al., 2016; Hales et al., 2021) | model input |
| literature correlation (upper bound) | correlation whose $D_0$ is printed as an upper bound (row A3-13) | bounding model input |
| literature value (single temperature) | single diffusivity at one temperature, no activation energy (row A3-20) | spot comparison only |
| modelling convention | value chosen by a modeller (buffer $D$, failed-layer $D$, instantaneous compact release, PARFUME test schedule) | reproduction of that model only |
| specification | design, nominal, test-procedure or benchmark-of-a-real-test specification | model input |
| synthetic benchmark | value defined only for a code-comparison case (CRP-6 cases 1 to 5 and 11) | code verification only, never a physical parameter |
| calculated | computed by a source (as-run neutronics, thermal analysis) or by this register | model input with the source's model uncertainty |
| estimate | author's inference or assumption (PIE failure counts, assumed 30 °C start, interpretive thresholds) | with caution; see the row note |
| evaluated nuclear data | ENSDF or JEFF-3.1.1 library value | model input |
| basis not stated | source does not say whether the value is measured, specified or calculated | context only until resolved |

### 0.4 Location convention

"p." is the printed page number on the page. "idx" is the 0-based PyMuPDF page index, so the PDF viewer page number is idx + 1. The page maps confirmed by the audits are: 2.pdf (TECDOC-978) offset not constant, read from each footer; 3.pdf (TECDOC-1674) idx = p. + 13; 5.pdf (Morris 2016) p. = 24 + idx; 6.pdf and 7.pdf (Collin 2016, identical content) p. = 378 + idx; 8.pdf (Hales 2021) p. = idx + 1; 4.pdf (Collin 2021) p. = idx.

### 0.5 Equation labels

No equation block was assigned to this deliverable, so the defining relations below carry register labels (R.1) to (R.8). They restate source equations or unit conversions; none is a new model.

## 1. Notation

| Symbol | Meaning | SI unit |
|---|---|---|
| $i = 1..5$ | layer index: kernel, buffer, IPyC, SiC, OPyC | 1 |
| $R_i$ | outer radius of layer $i$; $R_0 = 0$, $R_5 = R$ | $\mathrm{m}$ (tables in $\mathrm{\mu m}$) |
| $d_k = 2R_1$ | kernel diameter | $\mathrm{m}$ |
| $t_i = R_i - R_{i-1}$ | thickness of coating layer $i$ ($i \ge 2$) | $\mathrm{m}$ |
| $\rho_i$ | density of layer $i$ | $\mathrm{kg\ m^{-3}}$ (tables in $\mathrm{Mg\ m^{-3}}$) |
| $D_i(T)$ | effective diffusivity in layer $i$ | $\mathrm{m^2\ s^{-1}}$ |
| $D_{0,i,m}$, $Q_{i,m}$ | pre-exponential factor and activation energy of Arrhenius term $m$ | $\mathrm{m^2\ s^{-1}}$; $\mathrm{J\ mol^{-1}}$ (tables in $\mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$) |
| $D' = D/r_k^2$, $D'_0$ | reduced diffusivity referred to the kernel radius $r_k$ | $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ |
| $R_g$ | molar gas constant | $\mathrm{J\ mol^{-1}\ K^{-1}}$ |
| $T$ | absolute temperature ($T = \theta + 273.15$ with $\theta$ in °C) | $\mathrm{K}$ |
| $\Gamma$ | fast neutron fluence in units of $10^{25}\ \mathrm{m^{-2}}$ (cut-off stated per row) | 1 |
| $c(r,t)$ | fission-product concentration | $\mathrm{mol\ m^{-3}}$ |
| $\lambda_k$, $t_{1/2}$ | decay constant and half-life of nuclide $k$ | $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$; $\mathrm{s}$ |
| $y^I_k$, $y^C_k$ | independent and cumulative fission yield | atoms per fission |
| $\dot F$ | fission rate density | $\mathrm{fissions\ m^{-3}\ s^{-1}}$ |
| $N_A$ | Avogadro constant, $6.02214076\times10^{23}$ (exact, SI definition) | $\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$ |
| $S_k(r,t)$ | volumetric source of nuclide $k$ | $\mathrm{mol\ m^{-3}\ s^{-1}}$ |
| $M_{\mathrm{rel}}(t)$ | cumulative amount released through $r = R$ | $\mathrm{mol}$ |
| $f_{\mathrm{rel}}$ | release fraction as defined by each experiment (Eq. R.7) | 1 |
| $N_p$ | particles per compact or fuel element | 1 |

## 2. Defining relations

**(R.1) Arrhenius form.** IAEA (1997) Eq. (A-1), p. 435, idx 439:

$$
D_i(T) = \sum_{m} D_{0,i,m}\,\exp\!\left(-\frac{Q_{i,m}}{R_g\,T}\right) \tag{R.1}
$$

The tables print $Q$ in $\mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$ although the text of Eq. (A-1) and of Collin et al. (2016) Eq. (3) defines $Q$ in $\mathrm{J\ mol^{-1}}$, so $Q[\mathrm{J\ mol^{-1}}] = 10^3\,Q[\mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}]$ before use. Class: empirical correlation, exact as a definition. Limits: one term ("1T") when $m = 1$; $D \to \sum_m D_{0,i,m}$ as $T \to \infty$; each term vanishes as $T \to 0$. Two-term rows ("2T") are summed, which IAEA (2012, p. 571, idx 584) confirms is the intended reading for Cs in SiC.

**(R.2) Fluence-dependent Cs-in-SiC term.** IAEA (1997) Table A-3 footnote (1), p. 446, idx 450, and IAEA (2012) Eq. (10.9), p. 548, idx 561:

$$
D_{0,4,1}^{\mathrm{Cs}}(\Gamma) = 5.5\times10^{-14}\,e^{\Gamma/5}\ \mathrm{m^2\ s^{-1}},\qquad \Gamma \text{ in } 10^{25}\ \mathrm{m^{-2}},\ E > 16\ \mathrm{fJ} \tag{R.2}
$$

Exact as printed. Limit $\Gamma \to 0$ gives the zero-fluence value used by Collin et al. (2016) and Hales et al. (2021).

**(R.3) Reduced coefficient conversion.** IAEA (2012) Eq. (7.4), p. 318, idx 331: $D' = D/r_k^2$ with $r_k = 250\ \mathrm{\mu m}$, hence $D_0 = D'_0\,r_k^2$. Exact unit conversion. The kernel coefficients of IAEA (1997) Table A-1 are effective values "with respect to kernel radius r = 250 $\mathrm{\mu m}$"; applying them to a 350 $\mathrm{\mu m}$ AGR-1 kernel is an extrapolation.

**(R.4) Radii.** $R_1 = d_k/2$ and $R_i = R_{i-1} + t_i$ for $i = 2..5$. Exact.

**(R.5) Decay constant.** $\lambda_k = \ln 2 / t_{1/2}$ (exact) and $u(\lambda_k) = \lambda_k\,u(t_{1/2})/t_{1/2}$ (first-order propagation, approximate).

**(R.6) Fission source.** For a nuclide whose precursors are short-lived compared with the time step and the diffusion time, audit 07 Sec. 5.2:

$$
S_k(r,t) = \frac{y^C_k\,\dot F(r,t)}{N_A}\quad (0 \le r < R_1),\qquad S_k = 0 \text{ in the coatings} \tag{R.6a}
$$

Eq. (R.6a) applies only to rows whose `product_class` starts with "fission product". Ag-110m, Cs-134 and Eu-154 are fission-shielded activation products (`product_class` ends with "NO fission-yield source in STRATO"); their sources are capture terms on Ag-109, Cs-133 and Eu-153, whose cross sections are NOT VERIFIED (GAP-26). Their tabulated yields are listed for completeness only.

If a daughter $d$ of parent $p$ is tracked as a separate species, its source is

$$
S_d = \frac{y^I_d\,\dot F}{N_A} + b_{p\to d}\,\lambda_p\,c_p \tag{R.6b}
$$

never $y^C_d\dot F/N_A + \lambda_p c_p$, which counts the parent twice. Class: modelling rule (approximate, validity condition above). Precursor delays ($t_{99} = \log_2(100)\,t_{1/2}$ of the longest precursor) are 0.42 h (Cs-137), 0.48 h (Sr-90), 29.8 h (Kr-85), 36.5 h (Ag-111) and 221 h (I-131) (calculated in audit 07).

**(R.7) Release fraction definitions used by the data.** AGR-1: $f_{\mathrm{rel}}(t)$ is the cumulative measured release divided by the **calculated** compact inventory from as-run neutronics (Morris et al., 2016, p. 28, idx 4; Collin et al., 2016, p. 379, idx 1). "Matrix-corrected" values count release only after about the first 24 h at test temperature (Collin et al., 2016, p. 382, idx 4). Their denominator is the same calculated compact inventory (Collin et al., 2016, accepted manuscript p. 3; at the end of irradiation: Demkowicz et al., 2015, p. 58, and Stempien et al., 2023, p. 10); the value is the release from about 24 h at temperature to the end of the 300 h plateau (Collin et al., 2016, accepted manuscript p. 4), or to the end of the test where it was shorter (compact 6-4-3 ran about 400 h and compact 4-4-3 about 303 h, so E-014, E-036 and E-037 end at the plateau and not at the as-run end), which includes any later release from outside the SiC, so under premise BP1 it is a window upper bound of the intact-particle release and not a point measurement (Collin et al., 2016, accepted manuscript p. 6); under science design Section 1.1 it is context until the coordinator extends the bound definition. CRP-6: reference inventory is the inventory at the start of the heating test (IAEA, 2012, p. 552, idx 565). JAERI Table 4-9: fractional release per test, normalisation not restated in the audit notes.

**(R.8) Booth bare-sphere release (used only as a register check).** IAEA (2012) Eq. (10.7), p. 544, idx 557: $F = 1 - \frac{6}{\pi^2}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} e^{-n^2\pi^2 D' t}/n^2$. Series, truncated at $2\times10^4$ terms in the check.

## 5. Arrhenius register

All rows use Eq. (R.1). "2T" rows are the two terms of one summed correlation; separate "1T" rows with different temperature ranges (for example A2-11 and A2-12) are alternative branches and must not be summed. "none printed" means the table cell is blank. FRG, USA, Japan, UK and Russian Federation rows are kept separate even where the numbers coincide.

Using 8.3142 instead of 8.3143 changes $D$ at 1600 °C by $-1.2\times10^{-4}$ to $-3.8\times10^{-4}$ relative (calculated, check A). This is negligible against the order-of-magnitude uncertainty of the coefficients. Use the $R_g$ of the set being reproduced.

Schappel et al. (2020) is Nucl. Eng. Des. 357, 110428, doi 10.1016/j.nucengdes.2019.110428; the rows were read in the accepted manuscript (OSTI 1606816). The fit uses the AGR-1 heating-test release of compacts at 1600 and 1800 C (the compact 4-3-2 is named for 1800 C), the failed-fuel fractions 2.4e-4 (1600 C) and 1e-3 (1800 C) estimated from Cs release, a UO2 coefficient set for the UCO kernel, and the IAEA rows of the paper's Table 2 for the other layers. Rows S20-04 to S20-07 are hypotheses to explain the prompt Ag release (assumed Q or D chosen at two temperatures); the paper says the data cannot discriminate between them. The paper's own baseline (its Table 2) prints 5.8e-8 for the Cs kernel pre-factor (TECDOC-978: 5.6e-8) and 6e-8 for the Ag kernel pre-factor (6.7e-9 in its Table 6); these two entries are not recorded as rows.

### 5.2 UCO kernel coefficients: NOT VERIFIED

No UCO kernel diffusion coefficients were found in any source of the paper set. IAEA (1997, p. 437, idx 441) states that the US uses "a separate set of constants used for UCO kernels which are slightly higher than those for UO2" but does not tabulate them; IAEA (2012) contains no UCO diffusion data (keyword search, audit 04); Collin et al. (2016) and Collin et al. (2021) use UO2 values "due to lack of data for UCO kernels". Every AGR-1 kernel coefficient in this register is therefore a UO2 surrogate.

Check against the printed value of TECDOC-1674 Eq. (10.9) (printed p. 548): the sum for Cs in SiC at 1600 C and Gamma = 2 is 1.0113e-16 m2 s-1 (calculated), printed 1.011e-16 m2 s-1.

Reading note (verifier finding, resolved). The statement that the single term is "the published correlation" in the irradiation range is too strong: TECDOC-978 publishes the sum at every temperature. The irradiation-phase single term is a different published set (Collin et al., 2015, Table 2), and the TECDOC-978 sum differs from it by at most 5.3 percent up to 1250 C (calculated), so the choice of set is a documented decision under owner ruling 13 (decision 39), not a statement that the second term is absent from the literature.

| OPyC | dense pyrocarbon, 41.0 um (2.1), density 1.907 Mg m-3 (0.009), BAFo 1.019 (0.003) | Table 2 |

The PIE report does not call the PyC "LTI"; Collin INL/EXT-16-39548 (printed p. 2) states the PyC data are for LTI pyrocarbon, "the current type of PyC in TRISO fuel".

### 5.7 Class, published form and recommendation for every coefficient of arrhenius.csv


Class is exactly one of: AGR-1 experimental measurement; AGR-1-specific fitted correlation; published PARFUME correlation; transferred material correlation. No coefficient is an AGR-1 experimental measurement (no AGR-1 measurement of a diffusion coefficient was found).

Rules for use (audit 07): use the ground-state CFY for Kr-85 (2.8575e-3 for U-235), not the Kr-85m CFY; do not combine the Y-90 or Ba-137m CFY with a parent-decay source (Eq. R.6b); Ag-110m, Cs-134 and Eu-154 need activation sources, whose capture cross sections and isomeric ratios are NOT VERIFIED (Section 11).

Limit of the 4-2-2 history (verifier finding m4, resolved in the text): the trace of the figure gives 1600 C holds of 12.5 to 14.6 h (the three holds read as 12.5, 12.5 and 14.6 h from the trace, recorded as 13 h to keep the cumulative clock); the phase-4 ramp from 1150 C starts about 2 h earlier than recorded. Both lie inside the stated reading uncertainty of 8 h of this history.

Daily compact temperatures (Hawkes et al., 2012, used by PARFUME at the OPyC surface) are not in the paper set. Within a compact the temperature spreads "several hundred degrees" (Collin et al., 2016, p. 380, idx 2).

### 8.1 AGR-1 irradiation conditions (files `data/irradiation/*.csv`)

Tables 26a to 26f describe `agr1_irradiation_conditions.csv` (506 rows, ids IRR-001 to IRR-506), `agr1_burnup_by_cycle.csv` (2028 rows, IRRB-0001 to IRRB-2028) and `agr1_power_history_digitised.csv` (744 rows, IRRP-0001 to IRRP-0744). The CSV files are the source of truth. Evidence classes and statuses use the vocabulary of Section 0.2: `measured` marks as-manufactured characterisation means, `specification` marks pre-irradiation specification or plan values, `calculated` marks output of the INL as-run neutronics (JMOCUP, MCNP, ORIGEN) or thermal (ABAQUS) analysis, which is not a measurement and prints no uncertainty for the neutronics values; in rows IRR-003 to IRR-005 it also covers operational records (dates, number of cycles). Compact names follow the capsule-level-stack convention of Morris et al. (2016); 3-4-3 is capsule 3, level 4, stack 3.

Kernel inventory sources that differ between documents are all recorded: particles per Baseline compact are 4154 in Collin (2015) Table A-3 and Sterbentz et al. (2015) Sec. III, 4145 in Morris et al. (2016) as held in geometry.csv G-07, and 4152 (173 particles per layer times 24 layers) in the particle model of the physics analysis (Sterbentz et al. 2015, Sec. VII.A, PDF p. 7); the effect on the derived fission-rate density is 0.2 percent (4145) and 0.05 percent (4152).

### 8.2 Fission-rate density derived from published AGR-1 burnup (calculated)

No fission rate or fission-rate density is published in the AGR-1 documents opened. The generation input of the model may use a value derived from published values; it is then labelled **derived from published AGR-1 burnup (calculated)** and never measured, never published, never experimentally validated. No derived value is a data row; the Rust crate recomputes it from the rows (`Irradiation::derive_series`, checks DI.irr.inventory, DI.irr.step8, DI.irr.step9, DI.irr.derived-series).

Definition. FIMA is fissions per initial heavy-metal atom, so the fissions in a kernel up to a given burnup Bu (percent FIMA) are Bu/100 times the heavy-metal atoms N_HM,k per cubic metre of kernel. For ATR cycle n of 13, with the cumulative burnup Bu_n after the cycle (Appendix D of Collin 2015, rows IRRB-) and the cycle length EFPD_n (Table 2, rows IRR-006 to IRR-018): F_n = (Bu_n - Bu_(n-1)) / 100 * N_HM,k / (EFPD_n * 86 400 s), in fissions per cubic metre of kernel per second. The time average over the 620.2 effective full-power days is Bu / 100 * N_HM,k / (620.2 * 86 400 s).

Inventory (steps 1 to 4, calculated; masses of compact 3-4-3 from Sterbentz et al. 2015, rows IRR-500 to IRR-503; mass numbers used as molar masses, an approximation below 0.02 percent; Avogadro constant 6.02214076e23 per mol): 2.32627e21 heavy-metal atoms per compact; 5.6001e17 per particle (4154 particles per compact, a value derived by the source); kernel volume 2.23916e-11 m3 (diameter 349.7 um, row IRR-497); N_HM,k = 2.50097e28 m-3. A route that does not use the particle count (kernel density, uranium mass fraction, mean molar mass 237.39 g per mol) gives 2.4957e28 m-3, 0.21 percent lower.

Properties and limits. The burnup increments are differences of two printed two-decimal values, so each carries a rounding uncertainty up to 0.01 percent FIMA (up to 1.6 percent of the smallest increment). The Rev. 3 difference between Appendix D and Tables 3 and 4 changes the cycle-13 value by up to 0.05 / 1.17 = 4.3 percent for a single compact (the smallest cycle-13 increment is 1.17 percent FIMA, compact 3-4-1) and about 2 percent for a capsule average. The time base is the core-wide effective full-power day, not AGR-1 fuel burnup; the value is a cycle average, the rate varies within a cycle; the inventory of compact 3-4-3 is applied to every compact and variant; the calendar time of the irradiation is 1048 days and would give a value lower by the factor 0.592. A consistency check against the digitised capsule heat (200 MeV per fission assumed; ratio 0.93 to 1.20) confirms order of magnitude and units only and must not be used to tune either quantity. The calculated burnup agrees with the Cs-137 gamma measurement to C/E = 1.0013 +/- 0.0319 (rows IRR-505, IRR-506).

Offered by the generation input: user-supplied (no AGR-1 wording, no source row, not an AGR-1 irradiation condition); derived from published AGR-1 burnup (calculated), per capsule or compact, time-average or per cycle; an optional shape within a cycle from the digitised capsule heat history (digitised, proportionality of heat and fission rate assumed). Editing a derived value turns it into user-supplied.

Printed-table values (class "M printed table") and text statements ("M text", "M-UB") are kept apart from digitised values (R-dig, R-vis) in every table below through the Uncertainty / data class column and the Status column. The PARFUME column is model output printed or plotted in the same source; it is a calculated value, carried only for code-to-code comparison.

Applicability to a single intact particle (CSV column `particle_applicability`, B6 audit). Every AGR-1 value is a compact-level quantity: release from one compact of about 4145 particles divided by the calculated compact inventory, so one particle's full inventory is $2.4\times10^{-4}$ of the compact (MU-11). For STRATO, which models one particle, this means:

- Compacts with particles that have failed SiC (Tables 31 to 36, group "failed SiC") measure the failed particles, not diffusion through intact coatings. They apply to a STRATO failed-layer case only, and only after dividing by the number of failed particles of Table 38.
- For compacts with intact particles only, the compact release fraction equals the mean particle release fraction if all particles release alike. The matrix-corrected values of Collin et al. (2016) (release after the first 24 h) are the nearest AGR-1 analogue of a single intact particle. Under premise BP1 they remain a window upper bound of that release (class under science design Section 1.1: context until the coordinator extends the bound definition): the correction assumes that all release before about 24 h came from outside the SiC and none after it (Collin et al., 2016, accepted manuscript p. 6). Values without that correction include in-pile inventory already outside the SiC; Morris et al. (2016) state that Ag, Eu and Sr release was dominated by release during irradiation. The "<" values (evidence class "measured bound") bound the mean intact-particle release, include background and matrix contamination, and are inequality constraints, never point targets.

JAERI Table 4-9 values come from batches of about 100 loose particles without matrix (MU-12), which is closer to the single-particle setting, but the end-of-irradiation profile needed to simulate them is not given (GAP-24). CRP-6 values are fuel-sphere quantities.

### 9.1 Additional release measurements (Tables 31a to 31h)

Tables 31a to 31h render the rows E-157 to E-540 of `release_measurements.csv`; the row identifiers are identical in both places and the CSV is the source of truth. Ids E-316 to E-373 were withdrawn (interpolated or read between markers) and are never reused; the replacements are E-425 to E-540, read at the plotted markers. Time-dependent series are digitised from the stored vector coordinates of the figures and carry their reading uncertainty in the column `reading_uncertainty` (Section 0.6); it is not an experimental uncertainty, and the sources give no per-point experimental uncertainty (a general 5 percent systematic of the gamma counting for AGR-1, 10 percent for the AGR-2 totals of Table 31h). Kr-85 values marked N/D (none detected) are the class M-ND: the bound 1e-6 is the typical detection limit of the facility and not a limit measured for each test. Decision 43: AGR-1 publishes no tabulated release-versus-time data; Cs-137 is not reported by AGR-1 or AGR-2 (DATA UNAVAILABLE).

### Table 31d. AGR-1 capsule mass balance, summary table of 2023

Stempien et al. (2023) Table 11, printed p. 18. Differs from Table 31c by up to about 8 % in some entries; both are kept. For capsule 4 Eu-154 the primary source gives the upper bound <1.4E-4 (E-289) while this table prints 1.30E-4 (E-313) without <; E-289 is recommended for comparisons. The same Sr-90 and minimum-detectable-activity limits apply as in Table 31c.

### Table 31e. AGR-1 time-dependent cumulative release (digitised from Stempien et al. 2023, Figs. 9 and 12)

Four Ag-110m series and two Sr-90 series that can be identified individually (by end value in Table 14 and hold duration). The figures are vector drawings, so the points are the plotted markers (vertices of the plotted lines), recorded at their own times with the reading uncertainty stated in each row, as a subset of the markers where the note says so. These rows replace the earlier rows E-316 to E-348, several of which had been read off the connecting line at times where no marker is plotted (withdrawn). The other curves of these figures are not digitised.

### Table 31f. AGR-1 compact 4-4-2 loose particles at 1800 C (digitised from ORNL/LTR-2014/486 Fig. 4)

Cumulative release in particle equivalents of 75 particles without matrix. Includes five particles with failed TRISO. All 16 plotted markers of each series are recorded at their own times; these rows replace the earlier rows E-349 to E-373, which were interpolated between markers (withdrawn). The source's own conclusion is that the Ag and Eu release came mostly through intact SiC (printed p. 5, quoted in the rows). Eu-155 is in the legend of the figure and is plotted as a line of 13 vertices from about 47 h without markers; it is not recorded.

t = 691.4 h (elapsed time from start of heating) |  | digitised from the vector content of the figure: each plotted marker is a 6 pt image whose position is stored in the PDF page; marker centres read with the axes calibrated on the axis lines (0 to 700 h, 0 to 40 particle equivalents); reading uncertainty +/-0.05 particle equivalents (0.03 from the stored marker resolution, plus the rounding to three figures of values above 10 and a centre offset of about 0.04 at the zero line, found by the independent verification) and +/-0.3 h in time (the stored positions have a 0.12 pt resolution); the 16 plotted markers of the series are all recorded, the earlier rows between the markers (E-349 to E-373) were interpolated and are withdrawn; the marker times are probably the ends of the deposition cup collection periods (stated for the cups of the companion report ORNL/LTR-2014/485, not stated for this figure); unit is the average particle inventory (INL/ECAR-958 Rev. 2) summed over the sample, not a fraction per particle; time-dependent data were scaled by the average cup collection efficiency; Table 1 (printed p. 4) lists 10.0 % of the detected Eu-154 on the deposition cups and 85.8 % on tantalum parts, so the cup-based time dependence is scaled by a cup efficiency of about 10 % and is very uncertain in time; five particles had TRISO failure (three during heat-up and two at 1800 C); the Fig. 4 legend also lists Eu-155, which is plotted as a line of 13 vertices from about 47 h without markers and is not recorded; heating history in TH rows AGR1-LP-4-4-2 | 75 loose particles deconsolidated from compact 4-4-2, no matrix, individually gamma scanned, tested at 1800 C for about 650 h; nearest AGR-1 setting to a single particle, but five particles had failed TRISO and no end-of-irradiation profile is given; source conclusion (printed p. 5): the Ag and Eu release 'was greater than can be accounted for by release from the five particles with failed TRISO' and 'most of the silver and europium detected in the CCCTF can be presumed to have come through intact SiC layers' (leach-burn-leach of the particles before the test showed very little Ag or Eu outside intact SiC) | Hunn et al. ### Table 31h. AGR-2 UCO safety tests, total release at the end of each test (Sr-90 and Ag-110m)

Stempien et al. (2023) Table 15, printed p. 26; a different irradiation from AGR-1; the table states an estimated uncertainty of +/-10 %. UO2 compacts of capsule 3 and the Cs-134, Eu-154 and Kr-85 columns are not added. Compact 2-3-2 had one particle with a Mo-attack defect that released fission products (footnote c); it is labelled 'failed SiC' (nearest existing label) in E-406 and E-417.

What the checks establish:

- Schema (S): every CSV has one header row, a source column, a status column restricted to the three status values, unique identifiers and no ragged rows.
- Geometry (G): Eq. (R.4) recovers every thickness symbolically; all 80 tabulated outer radii are recomputed exactly.
- Decay (L): Eq. (R.5) holds for all 14 radioactive rows to $4\times10^{-7}$ relative; the uncertainty propagation is the exact first derivative.
- Fluence factor and Eq. (10.9) (F): the register's coefficients reproduce the printed check value $1.011\times10^{-16}\ \mathrm{m^2\ s^{-1}}$.
- Cross-set equality (X): the 27 "equals" claims linking Collin et al. (2016) and Hales et al. (2021) rows to IAEA (1997) rows hold exactly.
- Transcription (A): the 27 FRG reference values of audit 03 are reproduced to 4 significant figures, so no exponent or activation-energy slip entered the CSV.
- Benchmark (B): the two-branch Cs kernel row pair A1-01 + A1-02 reproduces both printed CRP-6 case 1 analytical values (0.4674 vs 0.4673; 0.99999959 exactly), while the single Table 7.1 branch gives 0.4616. STRATO must therefore use both Cs kernel terms for CRP-6 case 1.
- Source rule (Y): Eq. (R.6b) gives the cumulative yield at steady state; the alternative over-counts by exactly the parent yield.
- Histories (T) and release data (E): ramp durations, cumulative sums, printed totals, value ranges, failed-particle fractions and the Table 4-9 cell count all agree.
- B6 audit (V): an independent re-reading of all 81 Ag, Cs and Sr rows of IAEA (1997) Tables A-1 to A-5, Collin et al. (2016) Table 2 and Hales et al. (2021) Table 1 from page renders gives identical $D_0$, $Q$ and temperature limits; the gas constant per set is as printed; every CSV row carries an evidence class from the Section 0.2 vocabulary; every "<" release value is a measured bound; the 12 yield rows of Ag-110m, Cs-134, Eu-154 and their isomer partners are flagged as no fission-yield source. A mutation test (A3-16 $D_0$ changed from $6.8\times10^{-11}$ to $6.8\times10^{-12}$ in a scratch copy) makes the V transcription check FAIL, so it is not vacuous. ENSDF half-lives, decay modes, cut-off dates and all JEFF-3.1.1 yields were also compared cell by cell with a fresh LiveChart API download on 2026-11-06 (script `scripts/data_register/b6_nuclear_crosscheck.py`: 189 value checks and 15 activation-product class checks, 204 of 204 PASS; server `Extraction_date` 2026-11-06 on all 20 responses); see `data/reference/B6_audit_log.md`.

Limiting cases verified: $\Gamma \to 0$ in Eq. (R.2); Booth $F(D't = 0) = 0$ exactly; stable nuclides have $\lambda = 0$.

### 10.1 Rust data checks (crate `strato-data`)

```text
cargo run --locked --release --manifest-path crates/Cargo.toml -p strato-data -- check --repo .
```

The command reads the nine files, prints one PASS or FAIL line per check and a SUMMARY line, writes nothing and exits with status 1 on a failure. It reproduces every check of `D5_parameter_register.py` (and of the other audit scripts that read these files, `crates/strato-data/CHECKS.md`) and adds the family DI: class of every coefficient, phase, reference radius, fluence definition, the selection of the published coefficient (decisions 39 to 41, including the numbers of section 5.5), the columns of the release file, and the irradiation files with the derived fission-rate density (steps 1 to 9 of Section 8.2). On the files of this register the run gives `SUMMARY: ALL PASS (150 checks)`; the Python D5 script, run once for comparison, gives `SUMMARY: ALL PASS`. The Python script is not yet removed (decision 46).
